title: Ghost City Tours founder Timothy Nealon shares his favorite haunted place in America
excerpt: Ghost City Tours operates in over 60 locations across the country.
content:
Every city has a good ghost story or two, and what better way to learn about them than get your feet on the ground and experience them for yourself?

Timothy Nealon founded his company, Ghost City Tours, with the goal of entertaining and educating guests as they walk through a city.

“We take real people, real events, real history, real hauntings, and then we present it to the public in an entertaining manner while secretly educating them on the city and the culture of the people that they're surrounding themselves with,” Nealon told PauseRewind’s Elizabeth Stanton.

Ghost City Tours operates in more than 60 cities across the U.S., from New York to Los Angeles to Savannah, Philadelphia and beyond.

Nealon first got hooked on ghosts after visiting Gettysburg. “If you go there at the right time, the right place, and you go to the right place, it probably is not going to be long before you start believing in ghosts in some capacity, so that's kind of where my ghost journey startedBut you know, it's been a long journey. I've been interested in weird stuff the entire time.”

The business side came in after Nealon took a ghost tour in Savannah, Georgia and met the owners of that company. He offered his own business savvy to help grow the company, offering, “You'll make more money, and it'll give me something to do. And little did I know what Ghost City Tours would become.”

When it comes to building tours in each city, Nealon notes there is a lot of crossover between tour companies with stories, as some cities have more famous tales (think Marilyn Monroe haunting locations in Hollywood) that are used, but he and his teams in each city strive to offer as unique an experience as possible, often going beyond a ghost story into a city’s history.

“The ghosts like, I mean they're fun, they're interesting. Don't ever get me wrong, but to me, I get much more excitement out of finding like those little historical nuggets when we're researching tours. It doesn't even have to be ghost related,” Nealon said. “Sometimes you find stuff on a in a book or on newspapers.com or something like that, and you literally read it and you're like, holy s--t, this really happened? This person really existed? That's so much fun.”

Ghost City Tours relies on historical societies, talking with locals and people who work or live at or near the different stops, and digging through old books “like put the gloves on to turn the pages,” Nealon noted.

They also offer a variety of options in each city, from more family-friendly tours to adults-only tours and even haunted pub crawls.

And while ghosts are the draw, Nealon makes it clear that there is no guarantee you’ll have a spooky encounter.

“There are some people out there who think that oh, you have a ghost tour. I'm going to I'm going to see a ghost. I'm going to have a paranormal experience. Should we take ghost hunting equipment?’ And the answer to all those is no,” Nealon said.

He continued, “I mean, honestly, like chances are you're not going to have a paranormal experience. Chances are you're not going to experience a ghost, and there's really no point in bringing ghost hunting gear because one, that stuff doesn't detect ghosts, and two, it detects a lot of other stuff like cell phones or electric wires and all these other things. So you know, my advice to people is don't think that anything spooky is going to happen to you on a tour. Just go have fun, and if something does happen, that's great because every once in a while, one of our guides or one of our guests will be like, ‘Whoa, you're not going to believe what happened on a tour last night,’ and they'll describe something that genuinely seems paranormal.”

Nealon is a believer for sure though and confesses that his favorite tour is the first one he created, Savannah’s Dead of Night tour “because that's the first one that I wrote all the way back in 2012, and of course it's been modified since. We change things and new information comes to light.”

But he always goes back to his favorite place that got him into ghosts in the first place: Gettysburg.

“Not only is it a very haunted place, but for me, it has a lot of meaning because of what happened there,” he said. “We really don't have a lot of opportunities to go to a place like Gettysburg and walk in the same field where you know these men fought and gave their life for something they believe in. It's not an opportunity that Americans have every day, or at least you know unless you live close to one of those locations. So, being there, to me it's almost like a sacred location.”

To see if a tour is available near you, check out ghostcitytours.com
